new_profiler_stats_task_8.cpu_pct_interpretation: First time we have CPU data. Median 14% is LOW for a compute-bound bench — implies the benchmark is GPU/memory-bound, not CPU-bound. Max 106% (single core) happens in bursts (probably subprocess spawning for code execution). Prior 8 runs reported cpu_pct=0 in ALL samples due to Task 8 bug.
new_profiler_stats_task_8.swap_io_interpretation: Median sustained rate 141 MB/s is LOWER than the prior 431 MB/s wall-time-averaged estimate because the new profiler captures actual per-sample bandwidth, not amortized. Max 3768 MB/s is peak burst during allocation events. Mean 238 reflects real compute-time bandwidth with bursts and idle gaps. The 8-run 431 MB/s 'hardware constant' was calibrated against the wrong thing — it's a time-averaged throughput including idle time, not instantaneous bandwidth.
new_profiler_stats_task_8.phys_footprint_interpretation: Tracks model + Python heap + compressed pages, ~1 GB above metal_active_gb on average (the Python-heap + compressor overhead). Much more informative than the old rss_gb metric which dropped to 0.1 GB during runs.

niah_decode_task_10_active.goal_3_gap: 4K at 32.1 tok/s = 64% of target 50 tok/s; 16K at 16.5 tok/s = 33% of target. Goal 3 still unmet on 8-bit native 3-bit KV.
